task.title: Add jitter to payment retries
task.description: Retry storms align under load. Add randomized jitter to the existing payment retry backoff without changing the attempt limit.

current_proposal.summary: Revise payment timeout handling by changing the payment-client RetryPolicy from the default max_attempts=1 and jitter_ms=0 to max_attempts=3 exactly and jitter_ms=50 (at least 50), preserving only-Timeout retries, independently sampling bounded jitter per attempt and per payment/client, and testing the attempt cap, jitter floor, retry eligibility, decorrelation, and bounded delay.
plan_steps: Locate send_with_retries and RetryPolicy in payment-client and confirm the stored defaults max_attempts=1 and jitter_ms=0 and the rule that only SendError::Timeout is retried while upstream errors return immediately.

Change the payment-client RetryPolicy to max_attempts=3 exactly and jitter_ms=50, using the existing jitter_ms field; do not preserve max_attempts=1, do not exceed 3 attempts, and do not derive jitter from a backoff interval.

Ensure jitter is applied per retry attempt and sampled independently for each attempt, payment, and client, with each sampled value bounded between 0 and the configured jitter_ms inclusive so delays are non-negative and the added jitter across at most two retries is bounded by 2*jitter_ms.

Before implementation, search stored project records for any overall payment deadline or provider timeout; verify the bounded worst-case jittered retry time against any documented limit found, and if no such limit is found record that absence rather than assuming one.

Add or update tests verifying: max_attempts is exactly 3 and never exceeded, including success-after-Timeout-retry and exhausted-retry cases; jitter_ms is at least 50 and non-zero so constraint_cap_is_three_attempts passes; only SendError::Timeout is retried and upstream errors are returned immediately without retry; jitter varies per attempt and is independently sampled or decorrelated across separate payments and clients; sampled jitter is non-negative, does not exceed jitter_ms per attempt, and the worst-case total jittered delay for three attempts stays within any documented payment deadline or provider timeout found in stored records.

claims.statement: The payment-client default RetryPolicy is max_attempts=1 with jitter_ms=0 and therefore has no effective between-attempt retry delay; this proposal changes that configuration rather than modifying a pre-existing backoff delay. Checkable against the stored default-policy record and the payments-review decision record.

The proposal sets RetryPolicy.jitter_ms to 50, which satisfies the documented requirement of jitter_ms at least 50 and is not 0; no jitter is derived from any backoff interval. Checkable against the documented decision and the constraint_cap_is_three_attempts test record.

The proposal sets RetryPolicy.max_attempts to exactly 3, changing the default of 1 and not exceeding 3; send_with_retries retains the rule that only SendError::Timeout is retried and upstream errors are returned immediately. Checkable against the documented decision, test constraint, and send_with_retries behavior record.

assumptions: RetryPolicy.jitter_ms bounds or parameterizes the per-attempt jitter used by send_with_retries, so choosing 50 bounds the intended per-attempt jitter accordingly; this must be confirmed from the implementation before coding.
An independently sampled jitter source is available for each retry attempt, payment, and client.
uncertainties: The provided evidence does not specify a numeric overall payment deadline or provider timeout; stored records must be checked before implementation, and this uncertainty is not resolved by the evidence provided.

The provided evidence does not define the exact semantics of jitter_ms or the random sampling mechanism; the implementation must be inspected to confirm whether jitter_ms is an upper bound, fixed range, or other parameter.

If a documented deadline is found that conflicts with jitter_ms of at least 50 across three attempts, a further documented decision would be needed because the provided evidence does not settle that conflict.

items.description: Claim-2 is unsupported because the evidence describes send_with_retries governed by RetryPolicy.max_attempts and jitter_ms, but the default policy has max_attempts=1 and jitter_ms=0, so no existing backoff delay between attempts is established for the proposal to modify.

Preserving the currently configured attempt limit conflicts with the documented decision, because the current default is max_attempts=1 while the decision requires setting max_attempts=3 to fix payment timeouts.

The proposal does not specify that the existing RetryPolicy.jitter_ms must be set to at least 50, even though the documented decision requires jitter_ms of at least 50 and the existing test fails when jitter_ms equals 0.

Claim-3 describes deriving jitter from an existing backoff interval, but the evidence identifies a jitter_ms policy field set to 0 rather than any backoff interval from which a compliant nonzero jitter could be derived.

The proposed tests would verify that attempts equal the pre-change limit instead of verifying the required max_attempts=3 and the prohibition on exceeding three attempts, so they could lock in the current one-attempt default.

The plan contains no test preserving the existing rule that only SendError::Timeout is retried while upstream errors are returned immediately, so changing the retry timing could broaden retry behavior without detection.

The proposed tests do not verify that jitter is independently sampled or decorrelated across separate payments or clients, even though correlated retry bursts previously amplified an upstream slowdown into a full outage.

The proposal specifies no maximum jittered delay or test against an overall payment deadline or provider timeout, despite acknowledging that such a limit may apply, so sampled delays could extend timeout handling beyond an applicable bound.

assessments.note: No valid record directly states an existing backoff delay. The cited record states the default is max_attempts=1 and jitter_ms=0, so no between-attempt delay is established in the default flow.

No valid record states a backoff interval from which jitter is derived. The default jitter_ms is 0, while the decision specifies jitter_ms of at least 50 rather than the proposal's unspecified backoff-derived amount.

No valid record states the limit will remain unchanged. The current default is max_attempts=1, while the documented decision requires max_attempts=3, so preserving the current default conflicts with that decision.

Preserving the currently configured attempt limit conflicts with the documented decision, because the current default is max_attempts=1 while the decision requires setting max_attempts=3 to fix payment timeouts.

The proposal does not specify that the existing RetryPolicy.jitter_ms must be set to at least 50, even though the documented decision requires jitter_ms of at least 50 and the existing test fails when jitter_ms equals 0.

The proposed tests would verify that attempts equal the pre-change limit instead of verifying the required max_attempts=3 and the prohibition on exceeding three attempts, so they could lock in the current one-attempt default.

The plan contains no test preserving the existing rule that only SendError::Timeout is retried while upstream errors are returned immediately, so changing the retry timing could broaden retry behavior without detection.

The proposed tests do not verify that jitter is independently sampled or decorrelated across separate payments or clients, even though correlated retry bursts previously amplified an upstream slowdown into a full outage.

The proposal specifies no maximum jittered delay or test against an overall payment deadline or provider timeout, despite acknowledging that such a limit may apply, so sampled delays could extend timeout handling beyond an applicable bound.

revisions.summary: Revise payment timeout handling by changing the payment-client RetryPolicy from the default max_attempts=1 and jitter_ms=0 to max_attempts=3 exactly and jitter_ms=50 (at least 50), preserving only-Timeout retries, independently sampling bounded jitter per attempt and per payment/client, and testing the attempt cap, jitter floor, retry eligibility, decorrelation, and bounded delay.

chain.note: This run's events form a complete hash chain from genesis on their own: recomputing every record's hash and link from them alone verifies the run. head_hash is the hash of its last event. The chain is unsigned SHA-256. A successful check shows that the records received are internally consistent; it detects a change only against a hash obtained earlier, such as this receipt's head_hash or a published manifest. It cannot detect a run rewritten and re-hashed, a truncated tail or a deleted run, and it says nothing about whether the content is true.

receipt.proof_limitations: A proof marked valid means that Hyphae's verifier re-executed the request the proof sealed against its witness and accepted it at the anchor it was given (the pinned anchor wherever one is configured, always for the public snapshot). It covers the whole result of that request (for the sealed snapshot, the complete record list of the snapshot's project at that anchor), never a claim, even when the request's query is a claim's text, and a record's text is not byte-compared with the proof. A simulated proof checks nothing. Proofs do not establish that the content is true, relevant, or complete, or that a model reasoned from it.
